review_mode: Independent adversarial read-only review; no source edits, builds or numerical executions.

checks.detail: Cl_RterrG writes only RL[i][j] and RTerrG[i][j]. Cl_dTdtterr writes DT_TERR[i][j][k] and the same column's KST-1 slot. Cl_EpsB updates ref arguments bound to caller-local scalars, and Cl_Eps changes only by-value parameters and local variables. No shared scratch field, neighboring column write, reduction or utility side effect was found.

RTerrG and RL allocate a distinct row for each i. DT_TERR allocates a distinct vertical array for each (i,j). CreateArray invokes its factory separately for every element. The new loop assigns each i once, and its j loop is serial, so all destination elements have one writer.

Geometry, vertical integrals, temperature profiles, solar radiation, LStrich and upper emissivity preparation all finish before the new loop. The shared Wrad/CGp/Rp/Dz/Eps/Tab reference profiles are read-only during this phase. Each column calls Cl_RterrG before Cl_dTdtterr, preserving the RL dependency. TABS[1][1] is read here and is not a destination of either method.

Each column retains its own KST. Heating still runs from KST through Program.NZ and then copies KST into KST-1. The downward search still reads k-1 through KST-1 before decrementing its local kk. The existing initialization calls with NK=3 use the same full allocated Program.NZ profiles and the same later boundary limits as before; this patch does not substitute NK for NZ or change any range. The existing TABS level-10 access and valid allocated-profile requirements remain unchanged.

Parallel.For returns after its i bodies complete. The unchanged boundary copies begin afterwards and therefore read completed DT_TERR columns. The two existing boundary Parallel.For calls retain their ordering for each k. No asynchronous work escapes the body.

The loop uses the existing Program.pOptions and introduces no nested parallel calls in either terrestrial method. MaxDegreeOfParallelism=1 preserves a single active body. Column order may be scheduled differently, but there is no cross-column dependency or reduction in the changed phase. Scheduler overhead on one worker or small initialization domains is a performance question for the native paired tests, not evidence of changed numerical results.

The combined source contains both patches without changing either terrestrial method. PR #29 calculates one upper-emissivity tuple for each k and copies scalar values into the existing per-column arrays. Cl_EpsA reads the shared reference profile and does not use i/j in its calculations. Those serial copies finish before the terrestrial Parallel.For; no shared array alias or concurrent producer is introduced. The local double references in #29 belong to the completed producer phase.
